newsitem.title: UK: Goldsmith to keep up anti-Brussels fight in UK.
newsitem.headline: Goldsmith to keep up anti-Brussels fight in UK.

text.p: Sir James Goldsmith said on Tuesday that his Referendum party would remain a force in British politics and keep up pressure on the next government for a plebiscite on ties with Europe.

At his only news conference of the six-week election campaign, Goldsmith said his party had achieved its first goal of initiating an open debate on whether Britain should pursue tighter links with the European Union.
Asked how he would judge whether he had succeeded in Thursday's election, Goldsmith said he had no idea how many votes the Referendum party would poll.
But he said: "We have changed the debate. It'll be extremely difficult for the British people not to insist on the facts in the future. That is the first thing we want to be measured by."
Polls give the Referendum party about two percent of the national vote, but with pockets of greater strength in seaside seats where feelings over Europe's fishing policies run high.

Goldsmith, an Anglo-French billionaire who has spent about 20 million pounds ($30 million) on his crusade, quoted the Daily Telegraph as saying the Referendum party was on course to register the largest protest vote this century.

"This will make them, the new government, understand that there is a huge organisation out there and that we will not in future allow lies to be told," said Goldsmith, who believes successive governments have hidden their true intentions on Europe.
He said there was a need for the Referendum party to continue as "a channel of mobilisation" against any further steps towards a European superstate.
"I do believe that we need to continue as a movement so that if, in secret as in the past, politicians seek to give up our sovereignty, we will be there...
"Those who are with us... are very committed and will fight for the right to were doomed in Thursday's election. By surrendering determine whether this country is a nation or a province," he said.
Goldsmith said the ruling Conservatives sovereignty to Brussels without consulting the people, they had betrayed their natural supporters, he argued.
"They are gone, they have committed suicide.

"The Tories are dead. Their leaders have always said quite clearly that the Conservative Party is either a party of nation or it is nothing. They will pay the price for what they have done on May 1," Goldsmith said. ($1=.6165 Pound)
